new_statements.quote: d) pas de MR, aucune modification tonale morphologique : bangando. [...] Remarque 2. A la question, soulevée par Jacqueline THOMAS, de savoir si les différences de traitement tonal en fonction du type syllabique ne pourraient s'expliquer par la présence d'un accent dans les langues concernées, on doit répondre négativement : aucune ne présente actuellement de phénomène d'accent, d'intensité ni de longueur. L'hypothèse sera reposée en diachronie, lors de l'interprétation des correspondances phoniques (p. 345).
new_statements.translation: d) no MR [tonal modification rule], no morphological tonal modification: Bangando. [...] Remark 2. To the question raised by Jacqueline Thomas, whether the differences in tonal treatment according to syllable type might be explained by the presence of an accent in the languages concerned, the answer must be negative: none of them currently shows any phenomenon of accent, of intensity or of length. The hypothesis will be raised again in diachrony, in the interpretation of the sound correspondences (p. 345). [p. 345: 'The absence of accent in the present-day languages does not force this solution for Proto-Gbaya, but the hypothesis is conceivable at an earlier stage of the evolution.']
new_statements.citation: Moñino, Yves. 1995. Le proto-gbaya: essai de linguistique comparative historique sur vingt-et-une langues d'Afrique centrale (SELAF 357; Langues et cultures africaines 20). Paris/Louvain: Peeters. xiv+725 pp.
new_statements.locator: p. 285, ch. 16 'Récapitulation contrastive' (Morphologie: modification tonale), Remarque 2 following the table of tonal-modification areas whose list on the same page ends 'd) pas de MR, aucune modification tonale morphologique : bangando.'; cross-reference p. 345 Remarque
new_statements.reading: no word stress according to the source
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Opened and and read them visually (also cross-checked against). p. 285 (running head 'RÉCAPITULATION CONTRASTIVE 285') carries, exactly as quoted, the list item 'd) pas de MR, aucune modification tonale morphologique : bangando.' and 'Remarque 2. A la question, soulevée par Jacqueline THOMAS, de savoir si les différences de traitement tonal en fonction du type syllabique ne pourraient s'expliquer par la présence d'un accent dans les langues concernées, on doit répondre négativement : aucune ne présente actuellement de phénomène d'accent, d'intensité ni de longueur. L'hypothèse sera reposée en diachronie, lors de l'interprétation des correspondances phoniques (p. 345).' p. 345 ('CORRESPONDAN…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Bangando (like all 21 Gbaya languages Moñino surveyed) has no accent/stress, no intensity prominence and no length contrast; word prosody is carried entirely by a two-tone (H/B) lexical and grammatical tone system, and Bangando is singled out as the one language with no morphological tonal modification at all.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not mentioned (no stress of any kind is recognised).
new_statements.exceptions: None; the remark is categorical for all languages in the survey. An accent is entertained only as a possible pre-Proto-Gbaya diachronic stage (p. 345).
new_statements.domain_note: Statement is about the languages as wholes (word-level accent/intensity/length as a possible conditioner of tone sandhi across syllable types); it is a blanket remark in the comparative recapitulation chapter, not in the Bangando-specific chapter 15 (pp. 254-268, not obtained). Moñino's Bangando data: 800-word list, 200 sentences and a tale from informants at Yokaduma (Cameroon) originating from Pezam, Mikel, Yenga and Mbatika (pp. 51-52).
new_statements.identity_note: Moñino's 'bangando-ngombe' = Bangandu [bgf] = bang1347 (Glottolog lgcode on ref 116367); his data are from Bangando speakers of Cameroon (Moloundou area villages Pezam, Mikel, Yenga, Mbatika, interviewed at Yokaduma). The CAR Ngombe (nmj, Glottolog bookkeeping languoid ngom1265) is the same language; the ngom1265 audit folder holds the identical files and reached the same statement. Dialects Baagato [baag1244] and North Bangato [nort2776] are not distinguished in any source seen.
